parts.text:
14 Which expression for pressure is correct?
A
force per unit area
B
mass per unit area
C
mass per unit volume
D
weight per unit volume

hints: Notice the four options mix force, mass and weight in the numerator with area or volume in the denominator.
Recall the governing relation $p = F/A$ and that its unit is the pascal, $1 \text{ Pa} = 1 \text{ N m}^{-2}$.
Compare mass per unit volume with the definition of density to eliminate the density distractor before choosing the pressure definition.
walkthrough: Identify what is asked: the word definition of pressure, with choices using force, mass or weight over area or volume.
State the physical rule: pressure is the normal force acting on a surface divided by the area of contact, $p = F/A$.
Check units: force in $\text{N}$ divided by area in $\text{m}^2$ gives $\text{N m}^{-2}$, which is the pascal $\text{Pa}$ for pressure.
Compare the other phrases: mass per unit volume is density $\rho = m/V$, while mass per unit area and weight per unit volume do not match $F/A$.
Therefore force per unit area matches the definition and unit check. This is option A.

A.explanation: Pressure is defined by $p = F/A$, the normal force $F$ divided by the area $A$ it acts on.

B.explanation: Mass divided by area has units of $\text{kg m}^{-2}$ and is not pressure, which requires a force.

C.explanation: Mass per unit volume is the definition of density $\rho = m/V$, not pressure.

D.explanation: Weight per unit volume has units of $\text{N m}^{-3}$ and describes weight density, not pressure in $\text{N m}^{-2}$.
